findings.title: Task 8.5's live routing checks conflict with 8.6's changed-file assertion and omit the `concept` route
findings.description: 8.5 says "No argument and `comprehension` route to the comprehension flow (unchanged behavior)". Running that flow is not a no-op: `commands/analysis/understand.md` writes a new `9nn-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` per run, and `project-documents/user/analysis/` already holds 943/944, so two full runs produce 945 and 946. Yet 8.6 (line 346) asserts `git diff --name-only main` shows "only `commands/analysis/understand.md`, the generated concept, this slice's documents, and the DEVLOG". The design has the same tension (walkthrough steps 2 and 7), but the task breakdown gives the implementer no instruction to verify routing without completing the write, or to remove/account for the generated analysis documents — so 8.6 becomes unsatisfiable as written. Separately, 8.5 tests only three of the four routing cases; the `concept` → new flow case required by SC1 is absent, which makes 1.2's parenthetical "(Live selection behavior is exercised in Task 8.5.)" (line 97) inaccurate. 8.1 runs the concept flow but never explicitly confirms the `concept` argument was recognized. Fix: state in 8.5 that routing is observed at flow selection without a document write (or add cleanup/accounting), and add the `concept` → new flow case.

findings.title: Task 7 breaks the verify-after-author pattern and leaves SC4/SC10 output properties unverified
findings.description: Every authoring task from 1 through 6 is immediately followed by a verification subtask (1.2, 2.2, 3.4, 4.2, 5.3, 6.3). Task 7 (lines 258–296: `[INFERRED]` governance, output conventions, provenance block, cross-reference fix) has no paired verify — it jumps straight to the Task 8 walkthrough. The walkthrough does not close the gap: 8.1's check list (lines 308–317) mirrors design step 3 but omits three explicit success-criterion requirements — SC4's "dropped topics appear nowhere in the document — neither as content nor as gap markers" (only authored in 4.1 and checked as skill text in 4.2/5.3, never in the generated `000-concept.squadron.md`); SC10's "per-section sourcing over the full outcome set" (authored in 7.3, but 8.1 checks only the engagement-questions and inferred-claims lines); and SC10's "every `[INFERRED]` sentence satisfies the checkable rule" (the rule is authored in 7.1, never applied to output). These are named, mechanically checkable requirements with no verification point. Fix: add a 7.5-style verification against the design, and extend 8.1 with a dropped-topics scan, a section-sourcing outcome-set check, and an `[INFERRED]` rule check.

findings.title: Commit markers are rendered as checkboxes rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: All eight commit markers (`99`, `125`, `164`, `185`, `221`, `254`, `296`, `351`) are `- [ ] Commit: \`feat: ...\`` checkbox items, not plain bold `**Commit**:` lines. They do sit at working, tested points — each follows the paired verification subtask and a successful build — and the frequency (one per task, plus 9.3) matches CLAUDE.md's "commit at least once per task". The completed sibling breakdowns 361 and 362 use the identical checkbox form, so this is an established project convention rather than a defect; noted only as a deviation from the plain-line marker form.

findings.title: All 12 success criteria have authoring tasks, with no scope creep
findings.description: Traced each criterion: SC1→1.1/8.5, SC2→5.1/5.2/5.3/8.1, SC3→3.1–3.4/8.1, SC4→4.1, SC5→5.1/8.2, SC6→6.1/8.1/8.4, SC7→6.1/6.3/8.3, SC8→6.2/8.4, SC9→7.2/8.1, SC10→7.1/7.3/8.1, SC11→3.1/8.6, SC12→8.1/9.3. No criterion is orphaned. Tasks that don't map to a numbered SC (0 branch/premise checks, 2 preconditions and `/cf:onboard` boundary, 7.4 cross-reference fix, 9 close-out) all trace to the design's Technical Scope, Preconditions section, or Implementation Notes (line 448), or to project git/DEVLOG conventions — legitimate slice work, not scope creep. No Python, no `src/` edits, no new test infrastructure beyond the walkthrough.

findings.title: Sequencing is acyclic and Tasks 1–6 satisfy the test-with pattern
findings.description: Dependency order is sound: branch/premise (0) → selector (1) → preconditions (2) → sources (3) → mapping (4) → interview (5) → write contract (6) → governance/output (7) → walkthrough (8) → close (9). Forward references (1.2→8.5, 6.3→8.3) are informative, not circular. Each authoring subtask in Tasks 1–6 is immediately followed by a paired verification with its own success line, commits land after those verifications, and every one of the ~30 subtasks carries an explicit `Success:` criterion with concrete, checkable values (e.g. `grep -c '^## User-Provided Concept'` returns 1, `git diff` byte-identity). Task sizes (Effort 1/5–3/5) are independently completable by a junior AI.

findings.title: Proportionality and NFR handling fit the slice
findings.description: One task file for a markdown-only, effort-3/5 slice, matching the approved 362 breakdown's shape; no split into multiple task files, no overweight test tasks, and no steps dictating implementation detail beyond the design. The design restates no load/performance/latency NFR — the only "cost" mentions are bounded human interaction ("two short answers and one yes/no", line 39) and the read-discipline constraint "whole graph is never loaded" (line 333), which is a scoped-read rule verified by 8.6, not a load test. `tests/load/` does not exist and no load-test task is present, so no CI gating task is required either; 8.6's existing `ruff format --check` / `pytest tests/skills/` regression line is inherited from 362 and CLAUDE.md's build-after-changes rule, not an extra success-criterion test. Absence of load/CI wiring here is correct, not a finding.
